claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Florida
claims.text: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed Executive Order 26-202 on 6 October 2026 in Tallahassee, declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties (Baker, Bay, Calhoun, Columbia, Dixie, Escambia, Franklin, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Gulf, Hamilton, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Leon, Liberty, Madison, Okaloosa, Santa Rosa, Suwannee, Taylor, Walton, Wakulla and Washington) ahead of Tropical Depression Nine, which strengthened into Hurricane Isaias, directing the Florida Division of Emergency Management to stage preparedness resources including generators, fuel, flood barriers and sandbags.

claims.source_name: Office of the Governor of Alabama
claims.text: Alabama Governor Kay Ivey declared a state of emergency for 40 Alabama counties effective 7 October 2026 at 4:00 PM Central time ahead of Hurricane Isaias, ordered state offices and buildings in Baldwin, Coffee, Covington, Dale, Escambia, Geneva, Henry, Houston and Mobile counties closed beginning 9 October at noon Central, and, at the request of local officials, ordered a mandatory evacuation of non-resident tourists and visitors from Baldwin County south of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway (including Gulf Shores and Orange Beach) and from Dauphin Island in Mobile County.

Georgia Governor Brian Kemp issued an updated Executive Order on 8 October 2026 declaring a State of Emergency covering all 159 Georgia counties in preparation for Hurricane Isaias, letting emergency management teams position resources ahead of the storm's impact, with GEMA/HS activating the State Operations Center beginning the afternoon of 9 October.

NOAA's National Hurricane Center Watch/Warning Advisory Number 15, issued 4:00 AM CDT (0900 UTC) on 10 October 2026, placed post-tropical cyclone Isaias near 32.0°N 86.5°W, about 25 miles south-southwest of Montgomery, Alabama, with maximum sustained winds of about 35 mph, moving north at about 14 mph and expected to weaken slowly and dissipate on 11 October; all storm surge and tropical storm warnings had been discontinued with no watches or warnings in effect.

NOAA's National Hurricane Center advisory issued 11:00 AM EDT (1500 UTC) on 11 October 2026 placed the remnant post-tropical system about 180 miles northeast of Nashville, Tennessee (37.5°N, 84.0°W), with maximum sustained winds of about 25 mph, and forecast it to dissipate over West Virginia that evening.

description: Hurricane Isaias, the Atlantic season's first hurricane, made landfall near Destin, Florida on 9 October 2026, prompting state-of-emergency declarations across Florida, Alabama and all of Georgia. The storm weakened rapidly after landfall, and the US National Hurricane Center classified it a dissipating post-tropical cyclone over the southern Appalachians by 11 October. Florida's and Alabama's declarations covered the Panhandle and southern Alabama, including a mandatory evacuation order for non-resident visitors in parts of Baldwin and Mobile counties, Alabama; Georgia's governor activated the state's Emergency Operations Center statewide as a precaution. No death or damage toll specific to any of the three states has been confirmed by an authoritative government source cited here, though media reporting attributes several storm-related deaths and widespread power outages to the storm.

impact.summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis's Executive Order 26-202 (6 October 2026) and Alabama Governor Kay Ivey's proclamation (effective 7 October) declared states of emergency for 25 Florida and 40 Alabama counties respectively ahead of landfall, while Georgia Governor Brian Kemp's 8 October Executive Order declared a statewide state of emergency across all 159 counties and activated GEMA/HS's State Operations Center. Alabama's declaration included a mandatory evacuation order for non-resident visitors in parts of Baldwin County (south of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, including Gulf Shores and Orange Beach) and Dauphin Island, Mobile County, plus state-office closures in nine counties. NOAA's National Hurricane Center tracked the system weakening to a post-tropical cyclone by 10 October, moving inland through Alabama toward the southern Appalachians and forecast to dissipate; no state or federal agency cited here has published a confirmed death, injury or damage total for the storm.
